explanation: When bile channels get blocked (maybe by a gallstone or liver trouble), a yellow pigment called bilirubin can't escape properly. It builds up in the body and turns the skin and eyes yellow.

question: A client with advanced dementia who wanders at night is being checked into an assisted living facility that does not have a secure memory unit. What should the facility do?

options.A: Wait until the client's memory improves on its own
options.B: Deny admission because the facility cannot keep the client safe
options.C: Admit the client and just use door chimes for night safety
options.D: Accept the client and assign a private nurse paid by the family

explanation: You've got this! Facilities must match their care to what the client genuinely needs. Admitting a wandering client to an unsecure place creates a big safety risk.

question: When a registered nurse delegates a vital task to an untrained auxiliary worker who then causes harm, who is primarily held accountable?

options.A: The hospital security guard on duty at the front gate
options.B: The federal ministry of health in the nation's capital
options.C: The pharmaceutical company that manufactured the ward equipment
options.D: The supervising nurse who delegated the task inappropriately

explanation: Nurses remain responsible for ensuring that delegated tasks are appropriate for the qualification and competence of the worker. [learn more](GST321_U10_T5#GST321_U10_T5_h6)

question: As a nurse, why do you collect culture and sensitivity samples?

options.A: To lower the patient's elevated body temperature rapidly
options.B: To stimulate white blood cell production in the bone marrow
options.C: To flush toxic metabolic waste products out of the blood
options.D: To identify the specific pathogen and its drug susceptibilities

explanation: C&S tests help us pinpoint the exact germ causing trouble and find out which specific antibiotic will knock it out.

question: What is the best way for a nurse to find out how much pain a patient is feeling?

options.A: Asking the patient and listening to them
options.B: Looking at the size of the injury
options.C: Watching for changes in resting pulse
options.D: Checking lab results for inflammation

explanation: Pain is personal! Only the patient truly knows what they are feeling, so their word is always our best guide.

question: What pregnancy hormone is most closely linked to the timing of first-trimester nausea and vomiting?

options.A: Human chorionic gonadotropin
options.B: Follicle stimulating hormone
options.C: Thyroid stimulating hormone
options.D: Luteinizing hormone

explanation: Human chorionic gonadotropin peaks during the first trimester right when nausea and vomiting are usually at their worst. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T012#GNS226_U2_T012_h1)

question: Why is a study that just repeats common knowledge without any new angle considered weak?

options.A: It will automatically cause patients to experience adverse events
options.B: It requires too much expensive laboratory equipment
options.C: It is illegal under international medical guidelines
options.D: It fails to advance the existing body of professional knowledge

explanation: Correct! As nursing students, we want our studies to push the profession forward, not just restate things everyone already knows.

question: What is the main job of synovial fluid inside a joint?

options.A: To anchor teeth tightly into their jaw sockets
options.B: To reduce friction between moving bone ends
options.C: To replace damaged hyaline cartilage permanently
options.D: To supply rigid calcium to the outer bone shaft

explanation: You got it! Think of synovial fluid as the natural 'engine oil' of your joints, keeping movements smooth and pain-free.

question: Which nursing intervention is the best example of primary cancer prevention?

options.A: Teaching a patient how to care for a surgical wound after tumor removal
options.B: Helping a newly diagnosed patient manage chemotherapy side effects
options.C: Administering the HPV vaccine to a group of adolescent students
options.D: Scheduling a routine screening mammogram for a 50-year-old woman

explanation: Giving the HPV vaccine prevents a viral infection that can lead to cervical cancer, fitting the definition of primary prevention. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T12#GNS321_U1_T12_h2)

question: Which major health issue deeply affects young people worldwide?

options.A: Unplanned pregnancies and sexually transmitted infections
options.B: Advanced age-related joint degeneration
options.C: Chronic occupational lung diseases
options.D: Severe childhood developmental delays

explanation: Correct! Adolescents face serious reproductive health challenges, which makes targeted education and friendly services so important.

question: What is an early sign of developing shock that you should watch out for in trauma patients?

options.A: High urine output
options.B: Altered mental status and cool skin
options.C: Warm, flushed skin
options.D: Slow and deep breathing

explanation: You nailed it. When the body goes into shock, blood gets pulled away from the skin and brain, making the patient feel anxious or confused with cool, clammy hands.

question: Why do sexual partners sometimes need treatment too when a patient has an infection?

options.A: To prevent passing the infection back and forth between partners
options.B: To ensure the patient takes all prescribed medication on schedule
options.C: To strengthen the partner's immune system against viral mutations
options.D: To stop the partner from experiencing sudden hormonal imbalances

explanation: Spot on! Many infections don't show symptoms in partners, so treating both prevents the annoying cycle of passing it right back.

question: What does it usually mean if a baby's weight line drops downwards across percentiles on a growth chart?

options.A: Rapid acceleration of normal muscle mass
options.B: A normal growth spurt following a brief illness
options.C: Potential nutritional deficit or underlying health problem
options.D: An error in the initial recording of the birth weight

explanation: Spot on! A downward drop in weight percentiles is a warning sign that the baby might be falling behind due to illness or poor feeding.

question: What is the main difference between primary and secondary dysmenorrhoea?

options.A: Secondary dysmenorrhoea never involves cramping in the lower abdomen
options.B: Primary dysmenorrhoea is caused by abnormal growths in the uterus
options.C: Primary dysmenorrhoea only affects women over forty years of age
options.D: Secondary dysmenorrhoea is caused by an underlying pelvic pathology

explanation: Primary dysmenorrhoea has no structural cause, whereas secondary dysmenorrhoea stems from a specific disease process like fibroids or endometriosis. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T6#GNS216_U2_T6_h3)

question: Why do we use the nursing process, especially in busy places like the ICU?

options.A: To replace the medical diagnosis made by the primary physician
options.B: To reduce the total number of nursing shifts required per week
options.C: To provide a systematic approach for individualized patient care
options.D: To eliminate the need for written nursing care plans

explanation: Think of the nursing process as your trusty roadmap! It helps you organize your thoughts and give care that is uniquely tailored to each patient's needs. You've got this!

question: What is an immediate nursing task to take care of right after an ultrasound scan ends?

options.A: Send the ultrasound machine back to central sterilization
options.B: Flush the IV line with heparin
options.C: Check the patient's blood sugar every hour
options.D: Wipe away any leftover coupling gel from the patient's skin

explanation: Cleaning up the sticky gel shows good bedside manner and keeps the patient comfortable and clean.

question: How does the NAFDAC Yellow Form system mostly gather its safety data?

options.A: Mandatory daily electronic tracking of every patient
options.B: Telephone interviews conducted by pharmaceutical reps
options.C: Automated computer alerts generated by hospital pharmacies
options.D: Spontaneous reporting by healthcare workers

explanation: The yellow form system depends on caring clinicians and nurses voluntarily filling it out whenever they notice a strange reaction in a patient.

question: Which of the following describes a standing plan in nursing?

options.A: A sudden emergency order that is never used again
options.B: A standardized guideline used repeatedly for recurring situations
options.C: A one-time budget created for a hospital building project
options.D: A five-year goal set by the board of directors

explanation: Standing plans like hospital policies and standard operating procedures are designed to be used over and over for routine situations. [learn more](GST321_U1_T6#GST321_U1_T6_h5)

question: Why does an undescended testicle often lead to problems with future fertility?

options.A: The testicle fails to receive any blood supply throughout childhood and adolescence
options.B: Immune cells easily cross the blood-testis barrier and destroy the abnormal organ
options.C: The vas deferens naturally attaches to the wrong structure during development
options.D: Higher core body temperature inside the abdomen damages the delicate sperm-producing tissue

explanation: Testes need a cooler environment outside the main body cavity; staying inside the abdomen causes permanent heat damage. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h3)

question: What is the main goal of using a chest drain to remove air or fluid from the chest cavity?

options.A: It restores negative pressure to help the lung expand properly
options.B: It prevents the patient from coughing up mucus
options.C: It directly cleans the inner lining of the bronchial tubes
options.D: It stops the heart from beating too fast during stress

explanation: Spot on! When air or fluid gets trapped in the chest, it breaks the natural vacuum (negative pressure) and causes the lung to collapse. The chest drain fixes that vacuum.

question: Which of these features is typically seen in a female pelvis rather than a male pelvis?

options.A: A wide pubic arch
options.B: A deep, narrow cavity
options.C: Inward-projecting ischial spines
options.D: A heart-shaped pelvic inlet

explanation: Women have a nice wide pubic arch to help make room for a baby to pass through easily.

question: Why is folic acid routinely given to women who are planning to get pregnant?

options.A: To stimulate rapid bone growth and skeletal mineralization in the fetus.
options.B: To prevent neural tube defects in early fetal development.
options.C: To increase the total daily caloric intake during the first trimester.
options.D: To protect the mother from developing severe iron-deficiency anemia.

explanation: Folic acid is a superstar for early pregnancy! It helps the baby's neural tube close properly, long before many mums even know they are expecting.

question: While listening to a pregnant patient with a Doppler, you hear a rhythmic sound matching her pulse. What should you do?

options.A: Record this rate immediately as the baby's heart rate
options.B: Assume the fetus has severe bradycardia and prep for emergency
options.C: Recognize this is the maternal pulse and keep searching for the faster fetal heartbeat
options.D: Stop the assessment because the machine is broken

explanation: Great job! Maternal blood vessels run through the uterus, so you always want to double-check that you're counting the baby's heart rate, not mum's.

question: How do tele-ICU networks help improve critical care in remote regional hospitals?

options.A: By automatically discharging stable patients without staff help
options.B: By lowering the total cost of hospital room construction
options.C: By replacing physical bedside nurses with video cameras
options.D: By allowing experts to consult on complex cases remotely

explanation: Tele-ICU technology connects regional staff with distant specialists to guide care for unstable patients in real time. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T1#GNS321_U2_T1_h7)

question: Which physical check is a reliable sign of dehydration, especially in older adults?

options.A: Increased muscle tone in the upper arms
options.B: Dry mucous membranes inside the mouth
options.C: Cool skin temperature in the lower legs
options.D: Reduced skin turgor on the back of the hand

explanation: Skin turgor can be tricky in older adults due to aging skin, but checking inside the mouth for moisture is very reliable.

question: Why is it best to put easy, general questions at the very beginning of a survey?

options.A: To trick the participant into answering difficult items quickly
options.B: To ensure the statistical software can read the demographic data
options.C: To shorten the total amount of time needed for data collection
options.D: To help the participant feel comfortable and build trust

explanation: Starting with gentle, straightforward questions eases anxiety and encourages people to complete the rest of the questionnaire. Brilliant thinking!

question: What does resource mobilization in community health primarily involve?

options.A: Storing excess clinic drugs in a locked warehouse for emergencies
options.B: Gathering funds, supplies, transport, and personnel needed for the plan
options.C: Waiting for the federal government to supply all necessary equipment
options.D: Asking international donors to handle every single community project

explanation: Resource mobilization is the active process of securing all types of inputs—human, material, and financial—to execute a health intervention. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h5)

question: What are the smaller building blocks that join together to make proteins?

options.A: Nucleic acids
options.B: Simple sugars
options.C: Amino acids
options.D: Fatty acids

explanation: You can picture proteins like long chains made of individual Lego bricks—and those bricks are amino acids!

question: Why shouldn't a nurse just hand out a generic diet pamphlet and call it a day?

options.A: Patients refuse to read any written information while admitted
options.B: Dietitians forbid nurses from using printed instructional materials
options.C: Hospital pamphlets are always outdated and medically incorrect
options.D: Patients have unique cultural, financial, and physical backgrounds

explanation: Great thinking! No two patients are the same. Good nursing care means tailoring advice to fit what the patient actually eats, loves, and can afford. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T005#GNS227_U7_T005_h1)

question: What is the core message of the contingency approach to management?

options.A: Every hospital must use the exact same leadership rules
options.B: Financial incentives are the only way to motivate staff
options.C: Managers should never change their personal leadership style
options.D: The best management style depends on the specific situation

explanation: Contingency theory teaches that leaders must adapt their approach based on the unique demands of each scenario. [learn more](GST321_U1_T3#GST321_U1_T3_h5)

question: What does the 'impersonal' aspect of the Hot Stove Rule mean?

options.A: Discipline targets the behavior, not the person
options.B: Rules apply only to new nursing staff members
options.C: Managers should never speak to the nurse directly
options.D: Penalties are handed out by a computer program

explanation: Fair discipline focuses purely on what the worker did wrong rather than attacking who they are. [learn more](GST321_U1_T22#GST321_U1_T22_h3)

question: What are haematinics?

options.A: Enzymes that break down dietary proteins
options.B: Hormones that stimulate white cell immunity
options.C: Proteins that destroy old red blood cells
options.D: Nutrients needed for blood cell formation

explanation: Think of haematinics as the body's building blocks (like iron and vitamins) used to manufacture fresh, healthy red blood cells. You've got this!

question: What does 'therapeutic use of self' mean in nursing?

options.A: Using your personality and insights to connect with patients
options.B: Hiding all personal feelings behind a cold professional mask
options.C: Acting as a close personal friend outside of work hours
options.D: Sharing your own personal medical history with every patient

explanation: Spot on! It means using your own communication style and warmth on purpose to build trust and help the patient feel safe.

question: What kind of information does qualitative data primarily capture?

options.A: Standardized monitoring device readouts and scores
options.B: Exact physical weights and chemical lab values
options.C: Precise mathematical frequencies and statistical averages
options.D: Human experiences, feelings, and descriptive narratives

explanation: Qualitative data focuses on words and stories that explain what a healthcare experience feels like to a patient. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T1#GNS224_U2_T1_h2)

question: What is the main reason we report certain diseases to public health authorities?

options.A: To bill insurance companies for hospital admissions
options.B: To report specific illnesses to public health authorities
options.C: To track daily hospital staff attendance records
options.D: To update patient medical history in private files

explanation: You got this! Disease notification simply means letting health officials know about dangerous illnesses so they can jump in quickly and stop outbreaks before they spread. Great job!

question: How do A-delta nerve fibers behave differently from C nerve fibers?

options.A: A-delta fibers only react to emotional stress
options.B: A-delta fibers only work inside the brain and spinal cord
options.C: A-delta fibers carry dull aches over a long time
options.D: A-delta fibers are wrapped in myelin and carry sharp pain very quickly

explanation: Because A-delta fibers have a protective coating (myelin), they rush the message to your brain, giving you that immediate sharp sting right when you get hurt.

question: When is injectable artesunate preferred over oral malaria medications?

options.A: As a daily dietary supplement for pregnant women
options.B: When treating mild stomach ulcers caused by amoebas
options.C: In cases of severe, complicated malaria where oral intake is impossible
options.D: For routine outpatient prevention in healthy travelers

explanation: You got it! Severe malaria requires fast action through the IV or IM route because waiting on oral meds isn't safe for a very sick patient.

question: Which category of healthcare waste includes discarded scalpels and broken glass ampoules?

options.A: Sharps
options.B: Pharmaceutical waste
options.C: Pathological waste
options.D: General waste

explanation: Sharps are any objects that can puncture or cut skin, including needles, surgical blades, and broken glass vials. [learn more](GST114_U2_T7#GST114_U2_T7_h2)

question: What is a major use for 5-HT3 receptor antagonists like ondansetron?

options.A: Bacterial gastroenteritis
options.B: Chronic hypertension
options.C: Parkinson's disease tremors
options.D: Chemotherapy-induced nausea

explanation: That's right! Drugs like ondansetron are lifesavers for preventing and treating the heavy nausea caused by cancer treatments and surgeries. You're mastering pharmacology!

question: Why do we routinely check a laboring mother's blood pressure?

options.A: To estimate the exact birth weight of the infant
options.B: To detect signs of pre-eclampsia or hemorrhage
options.C: To measure the strength of uterine contractions
options.D: To check how fast the baby's heart is beating

explanation: Spotting dangerous BP spikes (hello, pre-eclampsia!) or sudden drops (bleeding) early lets us protect both mum and baby right away.

question: Why does a drop in estrogen during menopause lead to atrophic vaginitis?

options.A: It permanently closes the internal cervical os.
options.B: It thins the vaginal lining and reduces natural moisture and elasticity.
options.C: It triggers an allergic reaction to normal vaginal secretions.
options.D: It encourages the massive overgrowth of anaerobic bacteria.

explanation: You got it! Lower estrogen levels make the vaginal walls thinner, drier, and more fragile, which easily leads to irritation and inflammation.

question: What is one of the earliest signs that women with vulval cancer usually report?

options.A: Persistent vulval itching
options.B: Foul-smelling vaginal discharge
options.C: Sudden complete hair loss
options.D: Heavy lower abdominal cramping

explanation: You nailed it! Long-lasting, stubborn itching (pruritus) of the vulva is a major warning sign that brings patients to the clinic.

question: Why do simple wellness talks or self-care lectures often fail to fix heavy nurse burnout on a hospital ward?

options.A: Nurses already know everything about relaxation techniques from basic school
options.B: Burnout is primarily an organizational issue caused by heavy workloads and poor support
options.C: Self-care workshops always increase the physical stress of working night shifts
options.D: Attending wellness lectures is legally considered part of unpaid overtime

explanation: Telling an exhausted nurse to 'just relax' won't solve unsafe staffing ratios, endless shifts, or lack of equipment. The root cause is the work environment itself!

question: How does a 'liver enzyme inducer' medication affect other drugs in the body?

options.A: It increases the speed at which the liver breaks down certain drugs
options.B: It completely shuts down all metabolic processes in the liver
options.C: It turns oral medications into inactive substances in the stomach
options.D: It prevents the kidneys from filtering waste products into the urine

explanation: An enzyme inducer basically pushes the liver's processing speed into overdrive, causing other medications to leave the system much faster and lowering their levels in the blood.

question: How does Root Cause Analysis differ from traditional blame-oriented approaches?

options.A: RCA takes place before the patient even enters the hospital.
options.B: RCA focuses on fixing broken systems instead of blaming individuals.
options.C: RCA ignores human mistakes completely and focuses only on finance.
options.D: RCA is performed solely by patients rather than healthcare staff.

explanation: Modern patient safety principles recognize that human error is usually a symptom of deeper, faulty system designs. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T9#GNS312_U5_T9_h4)

question: Which factor is a major warning sign for nutritional risk in hospitalized patients?

options.A: Involuntary weight loss
options.B: Sleeping on the left side
options.C: Preferring sweet drinks
options.D: Wearing loose clothing

explanation: Unplanned or involuntary weight loss is one of the strongest indicators that a patient is at high risk for malnutrition. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T001#GNS227_U5_T001_h3)

question: Which device delivers a shock to stop dangerous, irregular heart rhythms?

options.A: An infusion pump
options.B: A suction machine
options.C: A cardiac monitor
options.D: A defibrillator

explanation: Exactly! The defibrillator sends a quick electrical current to reset a chaotic heart back into a steady rhythm. You're mastering this! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T11#GNS321_U2_T11_h3)

question: Why is it important to talk through the exercise steps with your patient beforehand?

options.A: It forces the muscles to relax without any effort.
options.B: It reduces anxiety and encourages the patient to cooperate safely.
options.C: It replaces the need to check vital signs or pain levels.
options.D: It completely eliminates all physical pain from arthritis.

explanation: Communication is key! When patients know what to expect, they feel less anxious and can help you keep them safe.

question: Why is it dangerous to keep expired medication anywhere near active stock supplies?

options.A: It creates a high risk of accidentally administering degraded drugs to a patient
options.B: It automatically invalidates the expiry dates of neighboring boxes
options.C: It takes up space that should be used for cleaning supplies
options.D: It causes the electric lights in the storage room to flicker

explanation: Closeness to active stock increases the chance that a busy nurse will grab an expired item during an emergency. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T19#GNS122_U3_T19_h7)

question: Which of the following structures is part of the axial region?

options.A: The upper arm
options.B: The hands
options.C: The trunk
options.D: The lower leg

explanation: The axial region includes the head, neck, and trunk, while the limbs make up the appendicular region. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T4#GNS111_U1_T4_h2)

question: A nurse notices a patient's blood pressure dropping rapidly and calls the doctor using SBAR. What information should be stated in the Recommendation part?

options.A: What action or intervention is needed right now
options.B: A summary of yesterday's nursing shift notes
options.C: The patient's full medical history from childhood
options.D: The exact cost of the patient's hospital room

explanation: Correct! The 'Recommendation' is where you clearly state what you need done right now to help stabilize your patient.

question: A patient trapped under a heavy collapsed wall beam is experiencing which type of asphyxiation?

options.A: Environmental oxygen displacement
options.B: Upper airway foreign body blockage
options.C: Mechanical restriction of the chest
options.D: Cellular poisoning from toxins

explanation: When heavy debris presses on the chest, it physically stops the ribcage from expanding. That's a classic mechanical restriction!

question: Why is a non-competitive antagonist considered impossible to push out by just adding more agonist?

options.A: The antagonist creates a permanent physical wall around the cell
options.B: The antagonist breaks down all extra agonists in the blood
options.C: Changing the receptor shape prevents agonists from fitting regardless of concentration
options.D: The body immediately destroys any extra medication given to the patient

explanation: Imagine someone bending the lock out of shape—no matter how many keys you try to push in, none of them will fit because the lock itself is distorted!

question: What exactly is an element of cost in healthcare finance?

options.A: The price charged to a patient for bed space
options.B: A penalty fee paid for late supply deliveries
options.C: The total profit made by a hospital ward
options.D: A way to categorize and break down expenses

explanation: Think of cost elements as simple buckets or categories we use to group and track money spent on things like staff salaries and ward materials. You've got this!

question: A pregnant patient in her first trimester worries when she notices blue, prominent veins across her breasts. What is the best nursing response?

options.A: Explain that this is an abnormal sign caused by a sudden drop in systemic estrogen levels.
options.B: Advise her to wear a tighter compression binder to restrict blood flow and reduce vein swelling.
options.C: Refer her immediately for an ultrasound to rule out a vascular thrombosis in the chest wall.
options.D: Reassure her that increased blood flow to the growing breast tissue causes superficial veins to become more visible.

explanation: It's totally normal! Her body is pumping extra blood to the breasts to nourish the tissue, which makes those surface veins show up more clearly. A quick word of reassurance puts her mind at ease.

question: What do we call the breathing difficulty that gets worse when a patient lies flat?

options.A: Sudden breathlessness that occurs only at noon
options.B: Inability to speak full sentences due to pain
options.C: Breathlessness that worsens when lying flat
options.D: Shortness of breath triggered by cold air

explanation: That's orthopnoea! Patients naturally prop themselves up with pillows to catch their breath. You will see this often in heart failure cases.

question: When do hospital managers use a Cost-Minimization Analysis?

options.A: When evaluating the most expensive surgery available
options.B: When the outcomes of two treatments are completely unknown
options.C: When competing interventions produce identical clinical outcomes
options.D: When measuring patient satisfaction scores on the ward

explanation: If two drugs do the exact same job with the same results, you just want to find the cheapest one. That is what cost-minimization is all about!

question: Which link in the chain of survival specifically addresses restoring a shockable heart rhythm?

options.A: Post-cardiac arrest care
options.B: Rapid defibrillation
options.C: Early recognition and prevention
options.D: Advanced life support medication

explanation: Defibrillation delivers an electric shock to treat life-threatening rhythms like ventricular fibrillation. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T1#GNS212_U2_T1_h2)

question: Where does personal protective equipment rank in the hierarchy of hazard controls?

options.A: Below administrative controls but above substitution
options.B: At the very bottom as a last resort
options.C: At the very top as the best choice
options.D: Right above elimination

explanation: PPE is the last line of defense because it does not stop the hazard itself, only protects the individual wearing it if other controls fail. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h6)

question: Why do many traditional taboos give the best pieces of meat to adult males instead of children?

options.A: Cultural hierarchy assigns priority foods to providers and leaders
options.B: Adult males require more physical energy to farm and hunt
options.C: Children's digestive systems cannot process animal protein
options.D: Meat spoils faster when eaten by younger family members

explanation: Traditional power structures often dictate that heads of households and male breadwinners receive the most prized food items first.

question: How do good health records help during a community disease outbreak?

options.A: They provide financial compensation to affected families.
options.B: They allow health authorities to trace the origin of cases and deploy targeted interventions.
options.C: They stop airborne infections by sealing folders tightly.
options.D: They automatically cure patients through digital profiles.

explanation: When an outbreak hits, clean records help public health teams track where cases are popping up so they can send vaccines and help right where it's needed most.

question: How does community-based rehabilitation help fight against social stigma?

options.A: By involving local leaders and educating the public about disabilities
options.B: By forcing communities to build expensive private hospitals
options.C: By restricting public gatherings for people with chronic illnesses
options.D: By hiding individuals with disabilities away from public view

explanation: Education clears up misunderstandings. When local communities learn together, they start seeing the person first, not the disability.

question: You want villagers to remember proper handwashing steps after an outreach. What is the most practical action to take?

options.A: Distribute illustrated posters showing handwashing steps to take home or place in public areas
options.B: Write the medical names of bacteria on a chalkboard during a one-hour lecture
options.C: Tell the villagers to memorize the steps by repeating them three times in silence
options.D: Ask the village head to verbally test every single resident on handwashing theory

explanation: Pictures speak volumes! Visual posters give people a daily reminder so healthy hygiene habits actually stick.

question: A patient is having a hard time buttoning their shirt and holding a toothbrush after a stroke. Who should step in to help with these daily tasks?

options.A: Physical therapist
options.B: Speech-language pathologist
options.C: Physiatrist
options.D: Occupational therapist

explanation: Occupational therapists are experts at helping patients regain fine motor skills for daily activities like dressing, eating, and brushing teeth.

question: A patient comes to the clinic with a sore on her labia that hasn't healed in four months. What should you suspect?

options.A: A normal hormonal change related to approaching menopause
options.B: A simple Bartholin gland cyst that will resolve on its own
options.C: A potential malignant vulval lesion requiring a biopsy
options.D: An acute yeast infection that needs oral antifungal medication

explanation: Spot on! Any sore or ulcer down there that refuses to heal after weeks must be checked for cancer through a biopsy.

question: A junior nurse listens to an experienced charge nurse mainly because 'that is how things have always been done here.' What type of authority is this?

options.A: Expert authority
options.B: Formal authority
options.C: Traditional authority
options.D: Coercive authority

explanation: You're doing great! When people follow rules or leaders simply out of long-standing custom and hospital culture, that's traditional authority at work.

question: After cleaning the skin with an antiseptic and before giving the numbing injection, what is the next important step?

options.A: Suturing the edges of the anticipated wound
options.B: Placing sterile surgical drapes over the patient
options.C: Applying direct pressure to collapse blood vessels
options.D: Allowing the antiseptic solution to dry completely

explanation: Patience is key! Antiseptics need a little air-drying time to actually kill the germs before the skin barrier is opened up.

question: Which nerve arising from the cervical plexus controls the diaphragm?

options.A: Sciatic nerve
options.B: Phrenic nerve
options.C: Musculocutaneous nerve
options.D: Vagus nerve

explanation: The phrenic nerve originates from cervical roots C3 to C5 and provides the sole motor supply to the diaphragm. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T26#GNS211_U3_T26_h4)

question: A nurse wonders if a self-care theory works for elderly patients in rural farming communities. Where does this research idea come from?

options.A: Biomedical laboratory equipment maintenance
options.B: Professional theories and conceptual frameworks
options.C: Hospital financial accounting records
options.D: Direct pharmaceutical marketing campaigns

explanation: Testing established nursing models on new groups of people is a fantastic way to grow our professional knowledge.

question: How can nurse burnout negatively affect counselling sessions?

options.A: It automatically increases clinic funding
options.B: It reduces the nurse's ability to show empathy
options.C: It removes all language barriers in the room
options.D: It improves the speed of patient discharges

explanation: When you're exhausted and burnt out, it's so much harder to find the emotional energy to deeply connect with your patients. Take care of yourselves, future nurses!

question: What is a major reason why patients struggle to take antiretroviral therapy over a long period?

options.A: Lack of available water in the community
options.B: Doctors changing the prescription daily
options.C: Daily pill fatigue and complex routines
options.D: Automatic expiration of medicine bottles

explanation: The requirement to take medications every single day for the rest of one's life often leads to exhaustion and missed doses. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T7#GNS216_U6_T7_h3)

question: At what specific time intervals is the Apgar score routinely performed on a newborn?

options.A: One and five minutes after birth
options.B: Immediately at birth and thirty minutes later
options.C: Ten and twenty minutes after birth
options.D: Every fifteen minutes for the first hour

explanation: The Apgar score is systematically calculated at one minute and five minutes after birth to evaluate the newborn's immediate adjustment to extrauterine life and response to resuscitation if needed. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T011#GNS226_U3_T011_h1)

question: What is a key characteristic of bone pain caused by osteomyelitis?

options.A: It completely disappears when the patient rests in bed
options.B: It shifts to a different bone every few hours
options.C: It is a constant, throbbing pain that worsens with movement
options.D: It only occurs when the patient eats cold foods

explanation: Bone pain from infection is typically deep, constant, throbbing, and intensified by physical activity or pressure on the site. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T17#GNS222_U1_T17_h5)

question: When dealing with adolescent confidentiality dilemmas, what is the nurse's main responsibility?

options.A: Instantly reporting every minor to local law enforcement authorities
options.B: Refusing to treat any patient under the age of eighteen years
options.C: Breaching privacy whenever a family member asks for details
options.D: Balancing client safety and health rights with ethical and legal realities

explanation: Nurses must carefully weigh a minor's right to privacy against legal duties and immediate safety concerns.

question: What is the very first thing you must do when starting a counselling session with a patient?

options.A: Building rapport and trust
options.B: Evaluating the final outcome
options.C: Setting strict behavioral rules
options.D: Discharging the patient

explanation: Before any healing conversation can happen, the patient needs to feel safe and welcome with you. Rapport is key!

question: Poor drainage and overcrowding in a neighborhood are examples of which part of the epidemiological triangle?

options.A: Environment
options.B: Agent
options.C: Immunity
options.D: Host

explanation: Well done! Surroundings, living conditions, and sanitation factors make up the 'environment' part of the triangle, which greatly influences how diseases spread.

question: What is the most important instruction for a patient after an IVP procedure is finished?

options.A: Take a strong diuretic medication to stimulate urine flow
options.B: Avoid eating any solid foods until the following morning
options.C: Drink plenty of fluids to help flush out the contrast dye
options.D: Remain completely on bed rest for the next twenty-four hours

explanation: Water is the best helper here! Drinking plenty of fluids helps the kidneys wash the remaining contrast dye safely out of the body.

question: Why do endocrine disorders often cause symptoms all over the body in different organs?

options.A: Endocrine glands are physically connected to every single organ in the human body
options.B: Hormones travel systemically through the bloodstream to reach many different target tissues
options.C: The liver automatically spreads hormone imbalances to the digestive tract
options.D: Hormone receptors are identical across all types of tissues and organs

explanation: Hormones are chemical messengers that travel far and wide through the bloodstream. If there's too much or too little of one, every organ that has receptors for it will feel the impact!

question: A patient with an external fixator on their leg says a metal pin site feels a bit tender. What should you do first?

options.A: Inspect the pin site for signs of infection, redness, or purulent drainage.
options.B: Remove the metal pin immediately to relieve the local pressure.
options.C: Document the finding as normal and schedule a follow-up in six months.
options.D: Apply a tight elastic bandage directly over the protruding pins.

explanation: Since pins go through the skin, they can easily invite bacteria in. Checking the site closely helps you catch early signs of infection or osteomyelitis. Excellent clinical thinking!

question: Which antenatal care service is most crucial for pregnant teenagers?

options.A: Intensive nutritional counseling and iron supplementation
options.B: Mandatory enrollment in adult literacy classes
options.C: Immediate scheduling of elective tubal ligation
options.D: Restriction of physical activity throughout all trimesters

explanation: Because teen moms are still growing and easily get anemic, good nutrition guidance and iron supplements are absolute top priorities.

question: A nursing mum wants steady, long-lasting energy for her daily chores. What should you recommend she eat?

options.A: Pure cooking oils taken directly by the spoonful
options.B: Salt-free butter eaten in large morning portions
options.C: Simple refined sugars found in carbonated beverages
options.D: Complex carbohydrates like yams and whole grains

explanation: Complex carbs digest slowly and steadily. Foods like yams and whole grains give you the sustained energy needed to care for a newborn all day long!

question: Which sign is a common indicator of food spoilage?

options.A: Bright clean color on fruit
options.B: Neutral scent from a can
options.C: Slimy texture on meat
options.D: Dry crisp feel on vegetables

explanation: A slimy feel, strange smell, or visible mold are classic signs that food has gone bad and should not be eaten. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T012#GNS227_U3_T012_h8)

question: A patient drops out halfway through a six-month nursing study on chronic pain. What is this called in research terms?

options.A: Testing
options.B: Attrition
options.C: Maturation
options.D: History

explanation: Attrition happens when participants leave or drop out before a study ends. It can mess up our data, so researchers always watch out for it!

question: Right after a multiple birth, which complication should a nurse monitor for most closely?

options.A: Gestational diabetes
options.B: Postpartum hemorrhage
options.C: Chronic hypertension
options.D: Hyperemesis gravidarum

explanation: You nailed it! Because the uterus worked overtime stretching for multiples, checking for heavy bleeding (due to poor contraction) is rule number one right after delivery.

question: Why must patients take off all jewelry and metal objects before a CT scan?

options.A: Metal attracts the magnetic radiation from the machine
options.B: Metal heats up dangerously during the scan process
options.C: Metal objects cause artifact streaks on the images
options.D: Metal interferes with the hospital Wi-Fi signals

explanation: Metal blocks X-rays completely and creates ugly, bright streaks on the scan that can hide important details. Always good to remember in clinicals!

question: A patient develops a fungal mouth infection (oral thrush) after taking strong antibiotics. Why did this happen?

options.A: Antibiotics caused the patient's immune system to stop producing white blood cells
options.B: The medication directly stimulated the rapid growth of fungal spores in the throat
options.C: The antibiotics destroyed the protective normal bacteria that usually keep the fungus in check
options.D: The patient consumed contaminated food while taking the prescribed pills

explanation: Strong antibiotics are like a bomb in the gut and mouth—they wipe out the good bacteria that normally keep fungi like Candida under control, letting the fungus multiply unchecked.

question: How do distribution bottlenecks contribute to micronutrient deficiencies in remote communities?

options.A: Government clinics ban the distribution of dietary supplements
options.B: Fresh, nutrient-rich foods spoil or become too expensive before arriving
options.C: Farmers deliberately hide vitamins inside processed food items
options.D: Families choose to stop eating locally grown grains completely

explanation: When transport fails, perishable protective foods fail to reach populations, leaving them with monotonous, low-nutrient diets. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T025#GNS227_U2_T025_h7)

question: What is the main difference between toxicokinetics and toxicodynamics?

options.A: Toxicokinetics tracks how the body handles a poison, while toxicodynamics tracks how the poison affects the body.
options.B: Toxicokinetics focuses on antidotes, while toxicodynamics focuses solely on initial absorption.
options.C: Toxicokinetics applies only to gases, while toxicodynamics applies only to swallowed liquids.
options.D: Toxicokinetics measures cellular receptor binding, while toxicodynamics measures kidney excretion rates.

explanation: Think of kinetics as what the body does to the poison (movement and ADME), and dynamics as what the poison does to the body (its impact on your tissues). You've got this!

question: Why is relying heavily on staff overtime a poor long-term way to save money?

options.A: Overtime is usually paid at a higher premium rate and leads to staff burnout
options.B: Overtime payments are never recorded in the unit operational budget
options.C: Working extra hours causes nurses to forget all their clinical training
options.D: Overtime hours are completely illegal under standard hospital labor laws

explanation: Constantly using overtime increases costs because of extra pay rates, and tired nurses are more prone to burnout and mistakes.

question: Which screening test uses a low-dose X-ray to spot tiny lumps and microcalcifications before anyone can even feel them?

options.A: Clinical inspection
options.B: Breast self-examination
options.C: Mammography
options.D: Ultrasound scanning

explanation: Mammography is fantastic for early catch because it spots microscopic changes long before your fingers ever could.

question: What is the literal meaning of the word 'pons'?

options.A: Bridge
options.B: Tunnel
options.C: Pillar
options.D: Gateway

explanation: The term pons translates to bridge, reflecting its anatomical job of connecting different regions of the brain. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T20#GNS211_U3_T20_h1)

question: Why does maternal hyperglycemia lead to macrosomia in the developing fetus?

options.A: Excess amniotic fluid stretches the fetal bones
options.B: Maternal fat deposits transfer directly to the baby
options.C: High fetal insulin acts as a growth promoter
options.D: The placenta grows larger to absorb extra water

explanation: Excess glucose from the mother triggers the baby to make too much insulin, and insulin acts like a growth hormone that causes the baby to grow unusually large. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T006#GNS226_U4_T006_h3)

question: About how much urine in an adult's bladder usually triggers the very first urge to go?

options.A: 1,500 to 2,000 milliliters
options.B: 3,000 to 4,000 milliliters
options.C: 200 to 400 milliliters
options.D: 10 to 20 milliliters

explanation: That's right! Around 200 to 400 ml of urine stretches the bladder enough to send those early 'time to pee' signals to your brain.

question: Why do patients receiving home care require different types of nursing care plans?

options.A: Because insurance companies refuse to pay for identical nursing tasks
options.B: Because a surgery recovery patient has different daily needs than someone with chronic heart failure
options.C: Because hospital policies dictate what happens inside private homes
options.D: Because every single patient shares the exact same medical diagnosis

explanation: Different health conditions require distinct nursing goals, monitoring schedules, and treatment approaches. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T8#GNS324_U1_T8_h1)

question: What is the key trait of a polyvalent nurse?

options.A: Focusing exclusively on surgical nursing care
options.B: Training across multiple clinical specialties
options.C: Specializing in pediatric medicine only
options.D: Working only in hospital management roles

explanation: Spot on! A polyvalent nurse is cross-trained in different fields, meaning they can comfortably move and work across various hospital departments.

question: What is the main job of progesterone on the muscular wall of the womb (uterus)?

options.A: It increases local blood clotting to prevent bleeding
options.B: It stimulates strong rhythmic pushes to expel the fetus
options.C: It triggers rapid thinning of the cervical opening
options.D: It relaxes the smooth muscle to prevent early contractions

explanation: Progesterone is the ultimate peacekeeper! It keeps the uterine muscles calm and relaxed so the baby can grow safely without early contractions.

question: You are feeding a patient who looks very tired and worn out. What is the safest way to handle their meal?

options.A: Allowing frequent rest periods and offering smaller, more frequent meals
options.B: Laying the patient flat in bed to conserve their physical energy
options.C: Mixing all the food together so it is easier to swallow quickly
options.D: Feeding the remaining food much faster to finish on time

explanation: Tired muscles make swallowing mistakes easy. Pacing the meal and serving smaller portions keeps your patient safe and energized.

question: Which of these is NOT one of the five core elements of post-abortion care?

options.A: Mandatory criminal investigation
options.B: Treatment of abortion complications
options.C: Contraceptive and family planning services
options.D: Post-abortion counseling

explanation: Correct! PAC is strictly about health, safety, and support—not punitive legal investigations. Our job as nurses is medical care.

question: Which brain chemical do minor tranquilizers like benzodiazepines boost to help you calm down?

options.A: Epinephrine
options.B: Acetylcholine
options.C: Dopamine
options.D: GABA

explanation: Benzodiazepines team up with GABA—your brain's natural calming chemical—to slow down nervous system activity. Excellent nursing knowledge to keep in mind!

question: Why is an independent double-check required for high-alert medications like insulin?

options.A: Hospital computers will crash if only one nurse logs into the system
options.B: These drugs carry a high risk of causing serious patient harm if misused
options.C: Double-checking makes the nursing shift go by much faster
options.D: Pharmacy departments refuse to dispense them to a single nurse

explanation: High-alert medications have a narrow safety margin, meaning even a small dosing mistake can lead to catastrophic patient outcomes. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T7#GNS112_U4_T7_h5)

question: Why is timely documentation of assessment findings important for patient care?

options.A: It is only required for billing and insurance purposes
options.B: It prevents patients from reading their own medical charts
options.C: It ensures continuity of care and accurate communication across shifts
options.D: It allows the nurse to leave the hospital premises much earlier

explanation: Prompt charting lets the next nurse or doctor know the exact status of the patient without relying on memory. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T1#GNS112_U6_T1_h7)

question: Which nursing action is most important for getting an accurate weight on a clinical scale?

options.A: Subtracting a standard clothing allowance from whatever scale value appears
options.B: Weighing the patient immediately after they have consumed a large meal
options.C: Ensuring the scale is calibrated and having the patient remove shoes and heavy coats
options.D: Using a spring-loaded bathroom scale brought from home for consistency

explanation: You got it! Checking that the scale is zeroed/calibrated and having the patient shed heavy outer garments ensures you are measuring the patient, not their jacket.

question: Which group of medications is commonly used as a short-term fix to manage annoying bleeding caused by progestin implants?

options.A: Strong narcotic pain relievers
options.B: Intravenous general anesthetics
options.C: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs)
options.D: Inhaled bronchodilator aerosols

explanation: A short course of NSAIDs like ibuprofen can work wonders in calming down irregular or heavy spotting linked to progestin implants.

question: A community health nurse notices three children from the same compound presenting with watery diarrhea and vomiting. What is the best immediate action?

options.A: Treat the patients, stabilize them, and report the suspected cholera cases to local authorities
options.B: Close down the entire primary health care clinic until next week
options.C: Tell the parents to stay home and wait to see if the symptoms go away on their own
options.D: Send a formal letter to an international health organization via postal mail

explanation: Great nursing care means treating the patient right in front of you while also sounding the alarm to protect the whole community from a potential outbreak.

question: What is the main goal of using the TNM staging system for lung cancer?

options.A: To determine the extent of disease spread and plan appropriate treatment
options.B: To measure the exact volume of air the lungs can hold
options.C: To calculate the patient's exact daily calorie requirements
options.D: To identify which specific type of cigarette the patient smoked

explanation: Brilliant! TNM helps the team figure out how big the tumor is, if it has reached lymph nodes, and how far it has spread, guiding the best treatment plan.

question: What happens to the ovary during ovarian torsion?

options.A: It bursts open and fills the pelvic cavity with blood
options.B: It shrinks completely and stops producing hormones
options.C: It twists on its supporting ligaments and loses blood supply
options.D: It swells up because of a severe bacterial infection

explanation: Ovarian torsion is basically like the ovary getting twisted on its stalk, which cuts off its blood supply. It's painful and needs quick attention!

question: Why are patients with weak chest muscles at high risk for getting pneumonia?

options.A: Decreased room ventilation directly introduces bacteria into the lungs
options.B: Their immune systems completely stop producing white blood cells
options.C: Their body temperature constantly stays above normal limits
options.D: They cannot cough effectively to clear mucus from their airways

explanation: Coughing is our body's way of sweeping out trash. Without a strong cough, mucus stays stuck, and germs love to grow in it!

question: Why are nurses uniquely positioned to perform effective infection surveillance?

options.A: They perform all terminal room cleaning procedures
options.B: They spend the most direct time at the patient's bedside
options.C: They are solely responsible for writing hospital policy
options.D: They process laboratory blood cultures in the hospital lab

explanation: Continuous bedside interaction allows nurses to spot early warning signs of infection long before lab results return. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h9)

question: What major nutrition challenges do dietitians frequently tackle in Nigeria?

options.A: Rare genetic disorders affecting bone density in infants
options.B: Protein-energy malnutrition and chronic lifestyle diseases
options.C: Severe vitamin toxicity from over-supplementation
options.D: High rates of scurvy among coastal fishing communities

explanation: Well done! Nigeria faces a double burden—dealing with undernutrition issues like kwashiorkor while also seeing a rise in lifestyle conditions like hypertension and diabetes.

question: When is the best time for a patient to give a sputum sample?

options.A: At any random time during the afternoon shift
options.B: Early in the morning right after waking up
options.C: Immediately after eating a heavy midday meal
options.D: Right before going to sleep at night

explanation: First thing in the morning is golden! Mucus collects in the airways overnight, giving you a rich, concentrated sample from deep in the chest.
